title: Bunkering & pollution
goal: Use must, mustn't and have to, and answer an inspector short and clear.

l20-01.text: The bunker barge is alongside and the hose is connected. Diego, before we start: scuppers?
l20-01.es: La barcaza de combustible está abarloada y la manguera conectada. Diego, antes de empezar: ¿imbornales?

l20-02.es: Todos los imbornales están tapados, jefa.

l20-03.text: Good. And the SOPEP locker is open and ready. We mustn't spill a drop.
l20-03.es: Bien. Y el pañol del SOPEP está abierto y listo. No se puede derramar ni una gota.

l20-04.text: Good afternoon. Lieutenant Chen, US Coast Guard. I'd like to watch the bunkering.
l20-04.es: Buenas tardes. Teniente Chen, Guardia Costera de los Estados Unidos. Quisiera presenciar el bunker.

l20-05.text: Of course, Lieutenant. Welcome on board.
l20-05.es: Por supuesto, teniente. Bienvenida a bordo.

l20-06.text: Cadet, a few questions for you. Where is the SOPEP locker?
l20-06.es: Cadete, unas preguntas para usted. ¿Dónde está el pañol del SOPEP?

l20-07.text: Next to the bunker station, on the port side.
l20-07.es: Al lado de la estación de bunker, por babor.

l20-08.text: What must you do if there's a spill on deck?
l20-08.es: ¿Qué tiene que hacer si hay un derrame en cubierta?

l20-09.text: Stop the bunkering, report to the Chief Officer, and contain the oil with the spill kit.
l20-09.es: Parar el bunker, avisar a la Primer Oficial y contener el combustible con el kit de derrames.

l20-11.es: No se puede tirar al agua.

l20-12.text: Correct. Short and clear. Who has to sign the bunker checklist?
l20-12.es: Correcto. Corto y claro. ¿Quién tiene que firmar la lista de verificación de bunker?

l20-13.text: The Chief Officer and the barge master.
l20-13.es: La Primer Oficial y el patrón de la barcaza.

l20-15.text: Well done, Diego. You answered like an officer.
l20-15.es: Bien hecho, Diego. Contestaste como un oficial.

screens.title: must · mustn't · have to · don't have to
steps: not necessary: You don't have to wait.
paras: must and have to mean almost the same. After he / she: has to.
But the negatives are very different: mustn't = prohibido; don't have to = no hace falta.
screens.avoid: You don't have to smoke (when you mean it's forbidden). · She must to sign. · She have to sign.

screens.q: Smoking on deck during bunkering is forbidden. You ___ smoke.
The Chief Officer ___ sign the checklist.
Is the life jacket necessary there?

screens.situation: Rolando wants to wash the oil into the sea.
screens.q: Stop him.

screens.title: Short answers to an inspector
paras: An inspector wants short, direct answers: the place, the action, the person. No long stories, no I think maybe…
If you don't know: I don't know, but I'll check with the Chief Officer. Never invent.
screens.avoid: Well, normally, in my opinion, maybe the locker is… · Yes, yes (without answering)

screens.q: What is the maximum rate? Write the number.
accept: three hundred

screens.title: mustn't: no T in the middle
paras: In fast speech it's short; listen for the n't at the end. It changes everything: must or mustn't.
